assessments.reasoning: The opening paragraph assigns a different component to each value specified by the index type and ties every such component to the denoted component type. The grammar requires an ordinal index type and permits a single-entry list, as demonstrated by both Example 1 declarations. The later paragraph rewrites a comma-separated list into an outer array and a nested component array. In Example 2 the outer Boolean value identifies an array component rather than a real component. The revised claim is restricted to an array declaration's own one-entry index list, so permits an explicitly nested component type without extending the outer mapping to the scalar type at the inner end.

limitations: The claim concerns logical component mapping. The component type can itself be an array type. The multi-index shorthand has separate nesting rules. This claim does not cover storage layout, packing, bound conventions, or conformant-array parameter rules.
Exact unextended ISO/IEC 7185:1990 online replica. The replica gives the printed text precedence where they differ. ISO 10206 Extended Pascal and product dialects require separate evidence.
